classes.label: Skull base, orbit or ITF; no residual vascularity
classes.criterion: Skull base erosion, orbit or infratemporal fossa involvement; no residual vascularity after embolization.

classes.label: Skull base, orbit or ITF; residual vascularity
classes.criterion: Skull base erosion, orbit or infratemporal fossa involvement with residual vascularity.
classes.why: Expect heavier bleeding from ICA branches; consider staging the resection.

classes.label: Intracranial with residual vascularity
classes.criterion: Intracranial extension with residual vascularity; suffix M for medial extension (toward the cavernous sinus and sella) or L for lateral extension (middle cranial fossa).
classes.why: Highest blood loss and residual rate; plan staged or combined surgery with neurosurgery.

classifications.caveats: Requires post-embolization angiography to grade. In the original series stage correlated with blood loss, need for staged surgery and residual disease.

classifications.name: Kadish staging of olfactory neuroblastoma (with Morita modification)
classifications.basis: Anatomic extent (Kadish et al. 1976), with stage D added for regional or distant metastasis by Morita et al. 1993 (modified Kadish).

classes.label: Nasal cavity
classes.criterion: Confined to the nasal cavity.

classes.label: Nasal cavity and sinuses
classes.criterion: Involves the nasal cavity and one or more paranasal sinuses.

classes.label: Beyond the sinuses
classes.criterion: Extends beyond the nasal cavity and sinuses — orbit, skull base, intracranial cavity (in the original system also cervical or distant metastasis).
classes.why: The commonest stage at presentation in most series; the stage does not separate cribriform erosion from brain invasion.

classes.label: Metastatic (Morita)
classes.criterion: Cervical lymph node or distant metastasis.

classifications.caveats: Kadish C is heterogeneous. The TNM system of Dulguerov ([[c.dulguerov]]) separates cribriform involvement (T2) and extradural intracranial or orbital extension (T3) from brain involvement (T4) and has correlated better with outcome in several series; [[c.hyams]] grade adds independent prognostic information.

classifications.name: Dulguerov TNM staging of olfactory neuroblastoma
classifications.basis: TNM system based on CT/MRI extent at the cribriform plate, orbit, dura and brain (Dulguerov and Calcaterra 1992).

classes.label: Nose and sinuses, sparing superior ethmoid
classes.criterion: Nasal cavity and/or paranasal sinuses excluding the sphenoid, sparing the most superior ethmoid cells.

classes.label: Reaches the cribriform plate
classes.criterion: Nasal cavity and/or paranasal sinuses including the sphenoid, with extension to or erosion of the cribriform plate.

classes.label: Orbit or extradural ACF
classes.criterion: Extends into the orbit or protrudes into the anterior cranial fossa without dural invasion.

classes.label: Brain
classes.criterion: Involves the brain.
classes.why: Resection includes involved dura and brain with frozen-section margins.

classes.label: Nodal metastasis
classes.criterion: Any cervical lymph node metastasis (N0: none).

classes.label: Distant metastasis
classes.criterion: Distant metastasis present (M0: none).

classifications.name: Hyams histologic grade of olfactory neuroblastoma
classifications.basis: Histology: architecture, nuclear pleomorphism, neurofibrillary matrix, rosettes, mitoses, necrosis and calcification (Hyams et al. 1988).

classes.label: Grade I
classes.criterion: Lobular architecture, pleomorphism absent to slight, prominent neurofibrillary matrix, Homer Wright pseudorosettes may be present, no mitoses or necrosis; calcification variable.

classes.label: Grade II
classes.criterion: Lobular, pleomorphism present, neurofibrillary matrix present, Homer Wright pseudorosettes may be present, mitoses present, no necrosis; calcification variable.

classes.label: Grade III
classes.criterion: Lobularity may be lost, prominent pleomorphism, matrix scant or absent, Flexner–Wintersteiner rosettes may be present, prominent mitoses, necrosis present, no calcification.
classes.why: High grade: more regional and distant failure; adjuvant chemotherapy is often considered.

classes.label: Grade IV
classes.criterion: Lobularity may be lost, marked pleomorphism, no matrix, rosettes uncommon, marked mitotic activity, prominent necrosis, no calcification.

classifications.caveats: Interobserver variation is considerable and many centers report low (I–II) versus high (III–IV). A high-grade tumor needs review against SNUC, neuroendocrine carcinoma and SMARCB1-deficient carcinoma.

classifications.name: Hardy (Hardy–Wilson) classification of pituitary adenomas
classifications.basis: Radiologic sellar floor change (grades 0–IV; Hardy and Vezina 1976) and extrasellar extension (stages A–E). The stages are given here as used in Wilson's 1979 modification (the Hardy–Wilson classification), which added stage 0 (no suprasellar extension) and divided parasellar extension into intradural (D) and extradural, cavernous sinus (E).

classes.label: Grade 0
classes.criterion: Sella of normal size and contour, floor intact.

classes.label: Grade I
classes.criterion: Normal-sized sella with focal bulging or asymmetry of the floor (tumor under 10 mm).

classes.label: Grade II
classes.criterion: Enlarged sella with an intact floor (tumor 10 mm or more).

classes.label: Grade III
classes.criterion: Localized erosion or perforation of the sellar floor.

classes.label: Grade IV
classes.criterion: Diffuse destruction of the sellar floor.

classes.label: Stage A
classes.criterion: Suprasellar extension into the suprasellar cistern.

classes.label: Stage B
classes.criterion: Suprasellar extension obliterating the recesses of the third ventricle.

classes.label: Stage C
classes.criterion: Suprasellar extension grossly displacing the third ventricle.

classes.label: Stage D
classes.criterion: Intracranial intradural parasellar extension (anterior, middle or posterior fossa).

classes.label: Stage E
classes.criterion: Extracranial extradural extension into or beneath the cavernous sinus.

classifications.caveats: A plain-film and CT era system: it describes bony remodeling well but cavernous sinus invasion poorly — use [[c.knosp]] for that.

classifications.name: AJCC T categories for maxillary sinus and nasal cavity/ethmoid carcinoma (8th ed.)
classifications.basis: AJCC Cancer Staging Manual, 8th edition, primary tumor (T) categories for carcinomas of the maxillary sinus and of the nasal cavity and ethmoid sinus (not mucosal melanoma, lymphoma or sarcoma). Codes here are prefixed Max- or NE- for the two sites. The 8th edition is still the current AJCC staging for these sites (the 2025 version 9 head and neck revision covered the nasopharynx).

classes.label: Maxillary T1
classes.criterion: Limited to the maxillary sinus mucosa with no erosion or destruction of bone.

classes.label: Maxillary T2
classes.criterion: Bone erosion or destruction, including extension into the hard palate and/or middle nasal meatus, but not the posterior maxillary wall or pterygoid plates.

classes.label: Maxillary T3
classes.criterion: Invades the bone of the posterior maxillary wall, subcutaneous tissues, floor or medial wall of the orbit, pterygoid fossa, or ethmoid sinuses.

classes.label: Maxillary T4a (moderately advanced)
classes.criterion: Invades anterior orbital contents, skin of the cheek, pterygoid plates, infratemporal fossa, cribriform plate, or sphenoid or frontal sinuses.
classes.why: Resectable for cure: plan orbital, pterygoid and skull base margins.

classes.label: Maxillary T4b (very advanced)
classes.criterion: Invades the orbital apex, dura, brain, middle cranial fossa, cranial nerves other than V2, nasopharynx or clivus.
classes.why: Usually not resectable for cure; resection only in selected cases (e.g. limited dural involvement).

classes.label: Nasal cavity/ethmoid T1
classes.criterion: Restricted to one subsite, with or without bony invasion.

classes.label: Nasal cavity/ethmoid T2
classes.criterion: Invades two subsites in a single region or extends to an adjacent region within the nasoethmoidal complex, with or without bony invasion.

classes.label: Nasal cavity/ethmoid T3
classes.criterion: Extends to the medial wall or floor of the orbit, maxillary sinus, palate or cribriform plate.

classes.label: Nasal cavity/ethmoid T4a (moderately advanced)
classes.criterion: Invades anterior orbital contents, skin of the nose or cheek, minimal extension into the anterior cranial fossa, pterygoid plates, or sphenoid or frontal sinuses.
classes.why: Endoscopic or craniofacial resection with dural margin when needed.

classes.label: Nasal cavity/ethmoid T4b (very advanced)
classes.criterion: Invades the orbital apex, dura, brain, middle cranial fossa, cranial nerves other than V2, nasopharynx or clivus.
classes.why: Usually not resectable for cure; resection only in selected cases.

classifications.caveats: Nasal cavity subsites are septum, floor, lateral wall and vestibule; ethmoid subsites are right and left. Staging needs MRI to separate tumor from secretions. N and M follow the general head and neck rules.

classifications.name: AJCC T categories for nasopharyngeal carcinoma (8th ed.; kept in version 9)
classifications.basis: AJCC Cancer Staging Manual, 8th edition, primary tumor (T) categories for nasopharyngeal carcinoma, staged on MRI. AJCC/UICC version 9 (Pan et al. 2024), used for cases diagnosed from 2025, is now the current edition for this site; it keeps the same T0–T4 categories with the wording clarifications given in caveats.

classes.label: T0
classes.criterion: No tumor identified, but EBV-positive cervical node(s).

classes.label: T1
classes.criterion: Confined to the nasopharynx, or extends to the oropharynx and/or nasal cavity without parapharyngeal involvement.

classes.label: T2
classes.criterion: Extends to the parapharyngeal space and/or adjacent soft tissue (medial pterygoid, lateral pterygoid, prevertebral muscles).

classes.label: T3
classes.criterion: Involves bony structures of the skull base, cervical vertebra, pterygoid structures and/or paranasal sinuses (version 9: unequivocal bone infiltration).

classes.label: T4
classes.criterion: Intracranial extension, involvement of cranial nerves (version 9: unequivocal on imaging or examination), hypopharynx, orbit (version 9: including the inferior orbital fissure) or parotid gland, and/or extensive soft-tissue infiltration beyond the lateral surface of the lateral pterygoid muscle.

classifications.caveats: The 8th edition replaced the older "masticator space" and "infratemporal fossa" terms with named muscles; version 9 words the T4 soft-tissue limit as the anterolateral surface of the lateral pterygoid. Version 9 also adds advanced radiologic extranodal extension to N3, splits M1 into M1a (three or fewer metastatic lesions) and M1b, and redraws the stage groups (stage IV is now metastatic disease only). T stage guides radiotherapy fields and chemotherapy, not primary surgery.

classifications.name: AJCC T categories for head and neck mucosal melanoma (8th ed.)
classifications.basis: AJCC Cancer Staging Manual, 8th edition, primary tumor categories for mucosal melanoma of the head and neck; still the current AJCC edition for this site.

classes.label: T3
classes.criterion: Limited to the mucosa and immediately underlying soft tissue, regardless of thickness or size.

classes.label: T4a (moderately advanced)
classes.criterion: Involves deep soft tissue, cartilage, bone or overlying skin.

classes.label: T4b (very advanced)
classes.criterion: Involves brain, dura, skull base, lower cranial nerves (IX–XII), masticator space, carotid artery, prevertebral space or mediastinal structures.

classifications.caveats: There is no T1 or T2: the staging itself encodes the aggressive behavior of all mucosal melanomas.

classifications.name: Simpson grade of meningioma resection
classifications.basis: Extent of removal of a meningioma including its dural attachment and involved bone (Simpson 1957); applies to all intracranial meningiomas, including [[dz.planum-tuberculum-meningioma]].

classes.label: Grade I
classes.criterion: Macroscopically complete removal including excision of the dural attachment and any abnormal bone (and the venous sinus if involved).
classes.why: Endonasally achieved for anterior skull base meningiomas by excising the dural base with the hyperostotic cribriform or planum bone.

classes.label: Grade II
classes.criterion: Macroscopically complete removal with coagulation of the dural attachment.

classes.label: Grade III
classes.criterion: Macroscopically complete removal without resection or coagulation of the dural attachment or its extradural extensions (e.g. hyperostotic bone).

classes.label: Grade IV
classes.criterion: Partial removal, leaving tumor in situ.

classes.label: Grade V
classes.criterion: Simple decompression, with or without biopsy.

classifications.caveats: Derived from a pre-microsurgical, pre-MRI series; in modern series the recurrence gradient between grades I–III is smaller, and WHO grade and molecular features (e.g. CDKN2A/B deletion, TERT promoter mutation) also drive recurrence.
